2026, the current year, since today is 2026-09-26 and Sep 29/Oct 20 2026 are the nearest upcoming occurrences

turn2.differences: The author's three conditions match my step-1 reading closely. The implicit points I noted (it must be a cycle object; the end-date change is the requested action, not an identifying condition) are correctly reflected by omission - they aren't separate matching criteria, just background facts. No meaningful gap between the author's conditions and the request as I read it.

ambiguity_effects.explain: In the abstract, this phrase could mean an issue titled exactly about checkout timeout, or more loosely any issue whose content concerns a timeout during checkout. In this data every issue that could plausibly qualify (WEB-1, WEB-3, GRO-1, PLA-1, MOB-1) has a title that literally begins "Checkout timeout on/during...", so both readings agree on which issues count. The ambiguity doesn't change any candidate's outcome here.

Absent a stated year, a reader must infer 2026 from today's date (2026-09-26). All dates in the actual records are 2026, so no candidate's classification depends on resolving this ambiguity - it just happens to not matter in this dataset.

ambiguity_effects.phrase: Fall Kickoff cycle (exact name vs. substring)
ambiguity_effects.explain: A careless or overly loose reading could treat "Fall Kickoff Retro" (c-name) as matching because it contains the words "Fall Kickoff", which would make it satisfy c2 and c3 as well and create a real conflict with c-target. But a careful reader settles this: "Retro" is a distinguishing word marking a separate, specific cycle (a retrospective), not the kickoff cycle itself, so the natural reading requires the name to be exactly "Fall Kickoff". This resolves cleanly rather than being a genuine toss-up, but the two readings do select different candidate sets if someone reads too loosely.

turn2.naturalness_note: The request reads like something a real Linear user would write - it identifies an ambiguous cycle name by giving a distinguishing start date and a specific issue/assignee pair, which is a realistic way to disambiguate among several same-named cycles across teams. No artificial or test-only phrasing is present.
